notes.meaning: John sees an angel sent from heaven with power to carry out God's judgment against the devil. The key and the great chain show that Satan is completely under God's control and cannot resist Him. Satan is a created being, so even an ordinary servant of God has enough power from the Lord to lock him away.

The angel overpowers the devil, using all his ancient titles to show that every kind of wickedness he represents is being stopped. He is bound for a thousand years so the church can experience a long season of peace and spiritual fruitfulness. God sets the exact limits on how far the enemy can go and how long his defeat will last.

differ.view: Believe the thousand years is a literal, future earthly kingdom that begins after Christ returns.
Believe the thousand years is a symbolic number representing the entire church age between Christ's resurrection and His return.

notes.meaning: Satan is cast into the deep pit, locked in, and sealed shut so that he cannot lead the nations astray with his lies. This divine seal makes his prison completely secure against any escape. When this long season of restraint ends, God's plan allows him to be set free for a short time to face his final ruin.

John sees thrones set up for God's faithful people who share in Christ's royal rule and honor. He notices especially the souls of martyrs and faithful believers who refused to bow to worldly powers or give up their faith. They are raised to life and enjoy high honor and victory with Christ throughout this glorious period.

differ.view: Hold that this is a literal bodily resurrection of believers who will reign visibly with Jesus on earth.
Hold that this reign is spiritual, describing the exalted life of departed souls with Christ in heaven or the spiritual renewal of the church.

notes.meaning: Those who do not belong to Christ do not share in this special honor and life while the thousand years last. The first resurrection refers to the blessed state of those who belong to Jesus and are given spiritual victory and joy. Faithful believers are singled out by God for special honor before the final judgment of all people.

God pronounces a special blessing of joy and holiness on everyone who takes part in this resurrection. The second death, which means eternal separation from God, has no claim or power over them at all. Instead, they serve near to God as priests and share in the royal honor of Christ's kingdom.

Once the thousand years are finished, God permits Satan to come out of the pit for a brief time. This release is not an accident or a victory for the devil, but part of God's sovereign purpose. It shows that evil will make one last desperate push before it is crushed forever.

Satan immediately returns to his old work of spreading lies and stirring up rebellion across the entire earth. He gathers a huge army of God's enemies, described with the ancient names Gog and Magog, showing how widespread the opposition is. Even after a long time of peace, human hearts that are not truly changed can still be led astray by the devil.

The vast army spreads across the land and completely encircles God's people and the beloved city, which represents the church. Yet before a blow can be struck, God sends down fire from heaven to wipe out the attackers completely. The Lord Himself fights the final battle for His people, proving that no weapon formed against them can stand.

The devil's long war against God reaches its absolute and final end. He is cast into the lake of burning sulfur to join the other enemies of God who were put there before him. His punishment is endless, bringing complete justice and ensuring that he will never harm God's people again.

John sees a massive, pure white throne that represents God's supreme holiness, majesty, and perfect fairness. The Lord Jesus sits upon it as the rightful Judge of the universe. His glory is so overpowering that the old physical creation seems to dissolve and vanish before His face.

Every person who has died, regardless of wealth, social standing, or age, is gathered before the Judge. God opens the books that hold a complete and perfect record of everything each person has ever done. Another book, called the Book of Life, contains the names of those who belong to the Savior and are saved by His grace.

differ.view: Teach that all people, both believers and unbelievers, stand before this throne, where the works of believers give public evidence of their saving faith.
Hold that this throne is strictly for the unsaved dead, since believers have already been evaluated for rewards at the judgment seat of Christ.

notes.meaning: No one can hide or be lost from God's summons, whether they drowned in the deep ocean or were buried in the earth. Death and the realm of the dead are forced to surrender every body and soul so they can be reunited for the judgment. Each person stands individually before God to give an account of their life.

Physical death and the grave, personified as the old enemies of mankind, are destroyed forever in the lake of fire. From this point on, dying and the separation of soul and body will never happen again. The second death is the terrible reality of eternal separation from God for those who refused His mercy.

The final outcome of every human life rests on whether one's name is found in the Lamb's Book of Life. Those who are not recorded there are cast out into the lake of fire because they rejected God's salvation. This solemn warning reminds everyone to put their trust in Jesus while the day of grace continues.
